These notes pertain to the Neotoma Aggregate Dataset "Adirondack water chemistry - PIRLA study lakes"
PIRLA = Paleoecological Investigation of Lake Acidification
Text from Camburn and Charles 2000 (page 10), which contains tables of chemistry data for the lakes in the aggregate dataset:
"Chemistry data come from several sources.  All values are arithmetic averages of measurements made on surface samples collected during the summer or fall.  Data for PIRLA Phase I lakes come from Charles (1982,1985) and RILWAS (Regionalized Integrated Lake Water Acidification Study; Driscoll and Newton 1985), and are further documented in Charles et al. (1990). Charles (1985) data are for 2 to 7 samples (usually at least 5) taken from 38 lakes during the summers of 1978 and 1979. The RILWAS data include samples from 7 lakes taken on 6 to 13 occasions from May through September 1984. The chemistry data for PIRLA Phase II lakes come primarily from the U.S. EPA=s Eastern Lake Survey (ELS), Phases I and II.  The ELS-I survey data are used for 45 lakes; single samples were taken during the fall of 1984 (Kanciruk et al. 1986; Landers et al., 1988).  ELS-II data were used for 28 of the study lakes; 1 to 3 measurements were taken during the fall of 1986 (Herlihy et al. 1991).  C.T. Driscoll (Syracuse University, personnel communication) provided supplemental data on pH, aluminum, and DOC for 13 lakes; samples were collected once from each lake during August and September 1988."
